#2075. Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

With promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

This also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

Milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

Rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

At times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

Tottenham Hotspur sensation Mikey Moore scored his first goal on loan at FC Koln in Friday's 1-1 draw away at Bayern Munich.

The 19-year-old opened the scoring with an expertly-taken finish, with the visitors ultimately hanging on for a shock point against the German champions.

The winger had been struggling before the international break, starting his loan with nine games across all competitions without a goal or an assist.

But Friday's game felt like Moore's true arrival, born off the back of his first goal for England's Under-21s during the international break.

The moment will have been significant at Tottenham, where discussion around the potential cancellation of Moore's loan had begun to grow in the fanbase.

The teenager is very highly rated in North London, and it is hoped that he will now start to thrive in the Bundesliga.

A first Bundesliga goal for Mikey Moore - and what footwork! 🤩The 19-year-old, on loan from Tottenham, gave Cologne a shock lead against Bayern Munich 💫 pic.twitter.com/tgNLlQnSIk

Interestingly, Moore has been deployed in a more central role in Rene Wagner's three-five-two system.

The 19-year-old played alongside Paul Okon-Engstier and Tom Krauss on Friday, offering late runs into the penalty box.

Moore was a danger throughout, and could well have ended the game with an assist to go with his goal after creating a big chance for Said El Mala.

He took five touches in the opposition box and completed three successful dribbles - the joint-most of anybody on the pitch.

Moore was fouled once and got his defensive work done, too, making a tackle, a clearance, five recoveries and winning five duels.

His goal was the standout moment, though. The talent made a great run forward and got on the end of El Mala's backheel, before taking the ball around goalkeeper Jonas Urbig with great skill and rolling the ball into the net.

Cologne-based outlet Kolner Stadt-Anzeiger were full of praise for Moore, and wrote: "An evening where almost everything went right.

"Involved in almost every dangerous attack. The goal drought was finally broken – and how! The young Englishman capped off a sensational counter-attack with his first goal for the club. In the end, his energy waned."

BILD were similarly complimentary describing Moore's goal as so "incredible" that "even many Bayern fans had to rub their eyes in disbelief".

Moore's big moment on Friday felt like one that could well be the start of a fantastic loan spell.

Speaking after the game, the teenager said: "I tried to stay calm and not panic. When I got the ball, I knew what to do – I was determined to score.

"We can take a lot of confidence from this game. It was a really strong performance. The lads gave it their all today."

It has been a difficult start to the season for Moore and Koln, but Friday's game could well trigger a transformation of their confidence.

#2070. GdS: Worth the price tag – how Moreira became ‘untouchable’ for Milan and Belgium

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the new busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

Immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby shows, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

He set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

Moreira is currently captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

Amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

With four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

The leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

#2069. Finance Guru raises 'question marks' over PIF's Newcastle future amid 'amazing' claim

PIF's future as Newcastle United owners is not guaranteed despite new audacious plans away from St James' Park.

That is according to former Manchester City financial adviser Stefan Borson, who exclusively told Football Insider that the owners' "appetite" for sport should be questioned.

PIF's future remains a talking point on Tyneside, and was especially major during the summer transfer window, as key players left on big-money deals.

Eddie Howe also stepped down as the Magpies went in a completely different direction, causing fans to raise questions over their ambitions.

However, the latest reports state that Newcastle's owners have been in advanced talks over plans for the building of a £1.3billion super stadium.

The news has certainly split opinion, and while it may suggest further investment from PIF, it does not completely rule out another takeover.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Borson has been cautious about ruling out PIF's exit, just because of new stadium plans emerging.

"I'm not saying that they are going to sell, but I do have a concern about the appetite of PIF to sport," he explained.

"They've moved the strategy a little bit away from sport. But personally, I don't think it changes much, right?

"Because right now, it is some nice drawings, some discussions with the sorts of people that you would want to discuss it with on viability.

"It's not impossible that PIF and the Reubens decide, 'Actually, this is an amazing opportunity to build in Newcastle,' and they do that and they fund it themselves with the banks that they have amazing relationships with.

"And make no mistake, Newcastle is not just PIF. The Reuben family are incredibly wealthy as well and very much involved at Newcastle and have stood their corner on every fundraising from memory.

"It's not impossible that they do decide to do this as part of a bigger project, but likewise I don't think it means there's no way that PIF would look to exit the situation. I think there are still question marks."

All signs currently point towards an entirely new stadium being built, rather than developing the famous one already standing on Tyneside.

This is obviously going to raise some concerns, with Newcastle having played their since 1892, but change is sometimes inevitable in the sport.

Borson has already told Football Insider that redeveloping St James' Park could end up being more expensive than building a new stadium altogether.

Newcastle's owners are incredibly smart, and if there is a cheaper way of doing business, you would expect them to go down that route instead.

#2068. Celtic will kick themselves when they see former outcast's 91% display vs Bayern Munich

Correspondent AUTHORITY NCTJ-qualified football journalist with experience at VAVEL, Hayters TV, SPORTbible, and Centredevils. FOCUS Premier League analysis, tactical deep-dives, and original opinion content across Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham, Manchester City, and Celtic. THE INSIGHT Evan utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified, high-speed reporting. He provides specialist tactical and analytical content to ensure fans get beyond the headlines and understand the full picture.

Former Celtic defender Jahmai Simpson-Pusey impressed again for FC Koln on Friday as they held on to a shock 1-1 draw at Bayern Munich.

The 21-year-old joined the German side permanently from Manchester City in the summer transfer window, moving in a £4.3million deal after impressing on loan in the second half of the season.

And the England youth international is already attracting interest from back in the Premier League, having got off to a superb start this season.

Simpson-Pusey's future could well have been at Celtic, if his brief loan spell had been handled differently.

The youngster arrived on loan in the summer of 2025 but was never really given an opportunity. He was left out of the Europa League squad and did even make it into the squad for the first eight Scottish Premiership games he was at the club for.

The defender would ultimately make just a single Celtic appearance before his loan was terminated in January.

A real explanation for Simpson-Pusey's struggle for minutes at Celtic has never really emerged.

The youngster was overseen by three managers during his brief time with the club, with none of them able to provide answers.

And those questions will only grow in intensity as the defender continues to impress in Germany.

Simpson-Pusey was excellent at the Allianz Stadium, though his job undoubtedly became easier when Harry Kane was forced off injured after just 20 minutes.

Still, the 21-year-old had to be alert throughout and was, completing 91 per cent of his passes and two successful dribbles.

The real highlight was his defensive work, however. Simpson-Pusey made a last-man tackle and two blocks - more than anybody else.

He made the most clearances of anybody, too, with eight, made two recoveries and won three of four duels on a superb night for him and Koln.

Simpson-Pusey's time at Celtic was his first taste of senior football away from Man City and it should have been a positive experience.

Yet it will ultimately go down as a period that the young defender had to get past to really find himself.

"Things just didn't go as planned. I was hoping to get some playing time," Simpson-Pusey said in April. "Basically, I did everything that was asked of me, and then at some point, I just wasn't getting any playing time.

"Then a new manager came in, and I didn't play for him either. I felt I'd done pretty well, especially since I wasn't playing in my usual position. Ultimately, it just wasn't the right fit between me and Celtic."

Amed SK will be looking to maintain their perfect home record in the Turkish Super Lig when they welcome Caykur Rizespor to Diyarbakir Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts sit third in the table with 23 points from 11 matches, while the visitors are 11th on 14 points, nine behind their opponents, although the visitors will arrive with renewed confidence after ending their winless run before the international break.

Amed had enjoyed an impressive run of results before their league outing against Galatasaray, remaining unbeaten in eight consecutive games (W6, D2) and winning three successive matches against Konyaspor, Samsunspor and Eyupspor.

Besnik Hasi's side beat Konyaspor 1-0 at home, secured a 2-1 victory away to Samsunspor and then produced an emphatic 5-1 win over Eyupspor, but that positive run was eventually brought to an end by Galatasaray.

Amed were far from overawed in Istanbul, scoring three goals in a thrilling 4-3 defeat, their second loss in 11 league matches, which has left them third with seven wins, two draws and two defeats from their opening 11 fixtures.

The hosts have been carried by their attack, scoring 28 goals during that period to become one of the most productive sides in the division, with only Fenerbahce (29) finding the net more times.

Their home form has been particularly impressive, as they have won all six of their league matches at Diyarbakir Stadium, scoring 19 goals and conceding just four, a run they will be confident of extending against a Rizespor side that has struggled for consistency.

This will be the first league meeting between these sides, although they have faced each other twice in the Turkish Cup, with both teams recording a home victory.

Rizespor, meanwhile, have endured a difficult spell, losing three consecutive league matches against Fenerbahce, Corum and Trabzonspor before drawing 0-0 away to Kocaelispor, following an earlier 2-2 stalemate with Goztepe.

However, Recep Ucar's side finally returned to winning ways before the international break, beating Erzurumspor 2-1 at home, with the victory ending a five-match winless run in the league and providing a much-needed boost ahead of their trip to Diyarbakir.

Their away form has been considerably stronger than their results at home, with three wins, two draws and one defeat from six road matches, although they are now winless in their last three away outings (D2, L1).

The Black Sea Sparrowhawks failed to score in an away game for the first time this season in the goalless draw at Kocaelispor, while the last time they failed to find the net in consecutive away matches was towards the end of the previous campaign, during a six-match winless run on the road.

Amed will be without Samuel Ballet, who is serving a suspension following his red card against Eyupspor, while Berat Percin and Veysel Sapan are also unavailable.

Ermal Krasniqi and Lumbardh Dellova are injury doubts, with both players facing uncertainty over their availability for Saturday's match, while Gokhan Gul could also be absent.

Ballet's suspension is a significant blow to Amed's attacking options, although Gift Orban is expected to lead the attack, with Dia Saba supporting him and Mbaye Diagne also in contention to feature.

Rizespor are expected to be without Can Bozdogan, Valentin Mihaila and Gennaro Borrelli, who are all dealing with injury problems.

Meanwhile, Khusniddin Alikulov remains sidelined as he continues his recovery from a cruciate ligament injury.

#2061. Di Marzio: Endrick and Tresoldi deals ‘not a financial issue’ for Milan – the situation

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.

Several reports and even the words of owner Gerry Cardinale have made it very clear that Milan plan to be busy in the winter mercato. The main target seems to be a forward to complete the attack, as well as a centre-back to help out the defensive department too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

“That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial issue,” he began.

“Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

“We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

“But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

“Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”

Brian Brobbey is currently sidelined through injury, but Sunderland could soon be without their star striker permanently.

Regis Le Bris is optimistic of the 24-year-old returning to the pitch quite soon, despite missing international duty with the Netherlands.

Brobbey has three goals to his name so far this season, all coming against Manchester City in an eight-goal thriller at the Etihad Stadium.

Sadly, he has struggled to stay full fit this term. But when he's firing on all cylinders, he's one of the most dangerous forwards in the division.

Many clubs were interested in his signature, including Chelsea and Manchester United, but he opted to stay at the Stadium of Light.

But if he can stay fit and prove himself in the run-up to the January transfer window, there could be an incredible move on the cards for the striker.

Another club interested in Brobbey during the summer were German giants Bayern Munich, though no official move was made.

Ordinarily, any centre-forward swapping their current club for the Allianz Arena would expect to play a back-up role to Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane.

The England international already has 10 goals and 11 assists in 16 games this season, adding to his 68 contributions in 2025-26.

However, Bayern confirmed in a new statement that Kane is likely to be sidelined for the "next few months" after going off injured against Cologne on Friday, 20 November.

It is understood that he has torn ligaments in his left ankle, leaving Vincent Kompany's side short of a world-class centre-forward.

Of course, nobody can say that Brobbey is at Kane's level, at least not yet, but he would be a decent option in the January window.

Football Insider understands that Sunderland wouldn't accept any offers unless relegation was a certainty, but that might be out of their control.

If the 35-time Bundesliga champions coming knocking for Brobbey's signature, there is no way that he'd be able to turn that opportunity down.

The Black Cats would be able to get a decent fee for him, maybe more than they would have done in the summer, but it would be a ginormous blow for Le Bris' side.

#2056. Genclerbirligi vs Gaziantep - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:48

Genclerbirligi will be looking to return to winning ways when they welcome Gaziantep to Eryaman Stadium on Saturday afternoon in the Turkish Super Lig.

The hosts sit 14th in the table with 11 points from as many matches, three points clear of the relegation zone, while the visitors are 16th and in the drop zone with eight points after losing seven of their opening 11 league fixtures.

Genclerbirligi head into Saturday's encounter after suffering a 3-0 defeat away to Besiktas in their last league outing, having been unable to build on the confidence gained from their emphatic 5-0 victory over Alanyaspor a week earlier.

That win was their biggest of the campaign and followed another 5-0 success against Karakopru Belediyespor in the Turkish Cup, but their return to league action in Istanbul brought them back down to earth as Besiktas scored twice before half-time and added a third after the break.

The Red-and-Blacks have now lost three of their last four league matches and won just one of their last nine, with their only victory during that period coming against Alanyaspor, while they have conceded 21 goals in 11 league fixtures, the third-highest total in the division.

Their defensive record has been a particular concern away from home, where they have conceded 14 times in five matches and scored just once, although their performances in Ankara have generally been more encouraging.

Genclerbirligi have collected eight points from six home league matches, winning twice, drawing twice and losing twice, and they have scored nine goals at Eryaman Stadium in the competition, with their 2-1 victory over Fenerbahce representing the highlight.

Bernd Storck's side will hope to avoid another winless streak by bouncing back immediately, with optimism stemming from their home results and the fact that they beat the visitors on this ground in their last meeting here, while they have also never lost to them at home (W4, D1).

Gaziantep, meanwhile, have endured a much more difficult spell, losing their last six league matches and failing to score in each of their most recent two outings.

Their latest defeat came at home against Kasimpasa, who secured a 2-0 victory with both goals coming before the break, while they had previously lost by the same scoreline away to Trabzonspor.

Those results followed defeats against Erzurumspor, Istanbul Basaksehir, Corum and Kocaelispor, leaving the Red-and-Blacks with just two wins and two draws from their opening 11 matches, alongside seven defeats.

The club subsequently parted company with coach Orhan Ak by mutual agreement following the loss to Kasimpasa, leaving Gaziantep to prepare for this fixture amid another managerial change.

Assistant coach Mustafa Aksoy oversaw the first training session after Ak's departure, but Volkan Demirel has been appointed as their new head coach, and the club will be hoping that a change in the dugout can bring an immediate response.

Genclerbirligi will be without Metehan Baltaci, who is suspended after receiving a red card for two yellow cards in the defeat to Besiktas, while Dimitrios Goutas remains sidelined with a serious knee injury that has ruled him out for the season.

Thalisson Kelven is also unavailable through injury, while Kevin Rodrigues remains sidelined and Peter Etebo is a doubt, leaving Storck with decisions to make in defence and midfield.

Pedro Pereira is also doubtful with a muscle injury, while Gokhan Akkan and Muhammet Ensar Cavusoglu are among the other unavailable players.

Gaziantep are expected to be without Kacper Tobiasz, who is recovering from a hamstring injury, while Nazim Sangare and Fuat Bavuk are also sidelined.

Sontje Hansen is another absentee, leaving the visitors without several options as they look to improve on a difficult run of form.

#2054. Virgil van Dijk's in-depth stats make Liverpool's decision for them

Correspondent AUTHORITY NCTJ-qualified football journalist with experience at VAVEL, Hayters TV, SPORTbible, and Centredevils. FOCUS Premier League analysis, tactical deep-dives, and original opinion content across Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham, Manchester City, and Celtic. THE INSIGHT Evan utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified, high-speed reporting. He provides specialist tactical and analytical content to ensure fans get beyond the headlines and understand the full picture.

Virgil van Dijk has suggested that he may be playing the final season of his Liverpool career.

The 35-year-old's contract with the Reds expires at the end of the season and it has been unclear if he will be offered a new one.

The Netherlands international remains a key part of Andoni Iraola's team and has been excellent so far this season alongside Jeremy Jacquet.

But Liverpool will be aware that Van Dijk's drop-off could be coming at any time over the coming months and years, with decision-makers keen to avoid a repeat of the Mohamed Salah situation.

The legendary winger's final year at Anfield was full of disgruntlement amid a public fall-out with Arne Slot, leaving his legacy slightly tarnished when he left in the summer.

With Iraola having replaced Slot, it seems unlikely that the same situation will take place, but the Reds cannot be too sure.

"I will forever be grateful for everything that happened over those years" 🥺Virgil van Dijk has his say on what his future holds with Liverpool 🔴 pic.twitter.com/Y6k8HpsBvC

Van Dijk joined Liverpool from Southampton in 2018 for £75million - a fee that was huge at the time, but has looked like a bargain in the years since.

The defender has consistently been among the world's best, and he continues to excel even in his mid-30s.

But there is an inkling that this could be his final year in the Premier League, and that his time at Liverpool may be drawing to a close.

"At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either," Van Dijk told Sky Sports in the build up to Sunday's game against Manchester United.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

"If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer."

Liverpool will not take great certainty in Van Dijk's comments, with the defender seemingly preparing for his departure.

It appears the Reds have a fight on their hands to convince the 35-year-old to stay, and it will be a worthy fight.

What has always been Van Dijk's best quality is his tremendous reading of the game.

Even at his age, the centre-back has the recovery pace to get back and cut out an attack by simply predicting where the pass will be.

Liverpool have averaged just one goal conceded per game while Van Dijk has been on the pitch this season, with the Dutchman perfect for such a high line.

Per game, the veteran is averaging 7.1 clearances, 1.10 interceptions, 3.5 recoveries, 0.5 blocks and 4.8 duels won, with a staggering 75 per cent win rate that ranks in the Premier League's 93rd percentile.

In the 2020-21 season, a Van Dijk in his prime performed worse in some of the same stats. He averaged just 4.12 duels won to a 63 per cent win rate, and only made 0.24 blocks.

It should be clear to Liverpool that the defender is far from finished, and that a new contract is a must.

#2051. Galatasaray vs Samsunspor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:49, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:30

Galatasaray will aim to stretch their lead at the top of the Turkish Super Lig table when they host struggling Samsunspor on Saturday afternoon.

The match has been moved from RAMS Park because of pitch problems and will now be played at Basaksehir Fatih Terim Stadium, with the league leaders given extra time to carry out maintenance and improvement work ahead of their upcoming UEFA Champions League fixture against Aston Villa.

Galatasaray went into the international break on a six-game winning streak in all competitions, a run that began with a 1-0 victory over Genclerbirligi before they beat Lille 4-2 in the Champions League and Fenerbahce 2-1 at home in the league.

The Lions then won 4-0 away to Konyaspor, beat Stuttgart 2-0 in the Champions League and edged Amedspor 4-3 just before the break, with their attacking output particularly impressive as they scored at least twice in five of those six matches.

In the victory over Amed, Galatasaray raced into a 3-0 lead through Rafael Leao's early strike, an own goal from goalkeeper Alban Lafont and Alexey Batrakov's effort before the hour mark, but they subsequently conceded twice before Baris Alper Yilmaz restored their two-goal cushion in the 80th minute, only for the hosts to concede again in stoppage time before holding on for the victory.

Okan Buruk's side have suffered just one league defeat this season, a 4-0 loss away to Trabzonspor, which has left them with 28 points from 11 matches, having also drawn 2-2 at home against Corum in their opening game of the campaign.

Keeping opponents off the scoresheet at home has been an issue for Cimbom, who have conceded in five of their six home league matches this season, including each of their last three.

Samsunspor won the last meeting against Galatasaray to end a nine-game losing streak in this fixture, but the visitors arrive in considerably worse form this season.

However, they received a much-needed boost just before the break, beating Konyaspor 1-0 at home to end an eight-game winless streak, which had been a club record.

It was also the first victory under Nenad Bjelica, who was appointed in October to replace Thorsten Fink, who was dismissed after nine months in charge following just one win in his opening seven matches.

Samsunspor are 17th on seven points, one place above the bottom and one point from safety, and while they finally recorded some positivity before the break, they travel to a venue where they have lost eight consecutive games, leaving them with a difficult task after the international hiatus.

Galatasaray have major absentees, with Victor Osimhen undergoing surgery on a loose fragment in his left knee after the Stuttgart game and expected to be out for several weeks.

Leao is also sidelined through injury, while goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir picked up a shoulder problem on international duty and is not expected to play, with Gunay Guvenc tipped to start between the posts.

Davinson Sanchez is also unavailable after withdrawing from Colombia's squad with a muscle problem, while Roland Sallai is sidelined through injury and Batrakov is also listed as unavailable.

Samsunspor have fewer concerns, although Celil Yuksel is sidelined through injury and Fatih Kaya remains a doubt.

Mohamed Bayo is expected to lead the attack, with Tanguy Coulibaly, Oskar Ohlenschlæger and Afonso Sousa providing support from the attacking midfield positions.

Gunay; Singo, Bardakci, Jakobs, Elmali; Torreira, Lemina; Akgun, Sara, Sane; Yilmaz

Bayazit; Mendes, Erakovic, Drapinski, Tomasson; Watt, Onur; Coulibaly, Ohlenschlæger, Sousa; Bayo

Galatasaray are without their main striker, first-choice goalkeeper and Leao, but they still possess considerably greater squad depth and arrive in strong form, which should prove too much for Samsunspor as we expect the league leaders to secure a comfortable victory.

#2048. Parma vs Roma - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:07, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 09:47

Still unbeaten in Serie A this season, free-scoring Roma will return to action with a trip to lowly Parma on Saturday evening.

Sitting third - just behind reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio - the Giallorossi averaged four goals per game as they posted three consecutive league wins before the break.

Despite suffering two agonising Champions League defeats in recent weeks, Roma have hardly faltered on the domestic front; they are one of only two teams still undefeated in Serie A, alongside surprise leaders Lazio.

Soon after swatting Cagliari and Udinese aside, the Giallorossi signed off for the international period with a comfortable 3-0 home victory over Sassuolo, in which rising star Rodrigo Mora scored for a third straight league game.

It was an increasingly rare clean sheet for a club boasting the most lethal attack in Italy's top flight: Roma are only the fourth team in 65 years to hit the 30-goal mark by Serie A’s 11th matchday.

Dating back to last term, Gian Piero Gasperini’s side have scored at least twice in all but one of their last 16 league fixtures, only failing to do so in Como, where Donyell Malen was sent off.

Allowed to roam freely into the opposition area, defenders have collectively contributed eight goals this season, easing any pressure on Malen, Mora and their fellow forwards.

Beginning the build-up to next month’s Derby della Capitale, Roma will now seek a fifth straight win over Parma, who they beat 3-2 on their most recent trip to Stadio Tardini, with Malen inevitably scoring twice.

In fact, Parma have lost 13 of the past 20 league meetings on home turf, so history will not be on their side this weekend.

The hosts have endured a rocky start to the season, already changing coaches, and new boss Alberto Gilardino only celebrated his first victory shortly before the break.

However, days after stunning Atalanta with a shock 3-0 win in Bergamo, his side were beaten by Bologna in the Derby dell'Emilia.

Parma were reduced to 10 men within eight minutes at the Tardini, after Abdoulaye Ndiaye was dismissed following a VAR review, and they ultimately ended up losing 2-1.

As a result, the Gialloblu sit just one point above the bottom three, with only eight points on the board so far.

The club’s second-highest Serie A scorer during his playing days, Gilardino has a more modest managerial record, and he surely faces another survival scrap after last term’s fruitless fight with Pisa.

Roma have welcomed Paulo Dybala and first-choice goalkeeper Mile Svilar back during the break, but the latter’s deputy Pierluigi Gollini remains a doubt after missing two games with a back injury.

Devyne Rensch (adductor) and Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) are still sidelined, but Gasperini should have everyone else available.

A sure starter up front, Malen sits joint-second in the Capocannoniere rankings with eight Serie A goals, and the Dutch striker also scored for his country in the UEFA Nations League last week.

Meanwhile, Parma will be missing Argentine forward David Romero, who sustained a serious shoulder injury against Bologna.

Diego Carlos is also struggling with a thigh strain, young defender Dominik Drobnic has been ruled out, and Ndiaye must serve a one-match ban.

In the absence of Romero, teenage starlet Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is another contender.

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Carboni; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Lontani, Toure

Svilar; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Molina, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Mora, Dybala; Malen

Roma can pick up where they left off before the break, as a limited Parma side will struggle to match their intensity and flair.

A fourth straight win in Serie A will warm the Giallorossi up for next week's tough trip to Paris Saint-Germain.

#2045. Napoli vs Torino - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:19, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 09:38

Separated by one place and one point, Napoli and Torino will return to Serie A duty on Saturday evening, when they meet at Stadio Maradona.

Both sides entered the international break on a grim run of form, sparking talk of another crisis for the hosts.

After setting out with lofty ambitions, Napoli sit 10th in Serie A after 11 matchdays and have lost three of their first four Champions League fixtures.

Struggling both in Europe and Italy's top flight, the Partenopei have won just five times across all competitions since Massimiliano Allegri succeeded Antonio Conte.

That represents their lowest tally of wins at this stage of a campaign since 2003, when they drew 10 of their first 15 games down in Serie B.

Before international football intervened, Allegri's men did earn some credit by holding league leaders Lazio to a 1-1 home draw, having previously suffered damaging defeats to Juventus and Porto.

While they ended their visitors' streak of six consecutive wins - and spurned several second-half chances to seize victory - Napoli ultimately slipped further behind in the top four race.

As a result, the Campanian club cannot afford to drop many more points at the Maradona, where they beat Torino 2-1 in March - their 15th win from the last 22 league meetings.

Torino's only two triumphs during that period both came in Turin, so their last top-flight win in Naples dates all the way back to 2009.

Like their hosts, it has been a mixed start to the season under new management: Ignazio Abate's reign began slowly, but Toro then posted their best run of league wins for six years, before suddenly faltering again.

Having previously taken maximum points from three consecutive games, Toro lost to high-flyers Como and Frosinone, then went into the break with a disappointing home draw against Lecce.

Nonetheless, the Granata have claimed 14 points from their first 11 games for the fifth time in six years, leaving them just one behind Napoli in standings.

So, with a win this weekend, Abate can surpass his former Milan coach Allegri, as ambitious apprentice meets fading master.

Napoli are still burdened by a significant absence list, but Allegri will have three players back at his disposal on Saturday: David Neres and Costantino Favasuli have recovered from muscular injuries, while Luca Marianucci has served his suspension.

Alisson Santos, Benoit Badiashile, Stanislav Lobotka, goalkeeper Alex Meret, captain Giovanni Di Lorenzo and former Torino skipper Alessandro Buongiorno are all unavailable.

Having starred in Belgium's big UEFA Nations League victory over Italy, top scorer Kevin De Bruyne will aim to build on his six goal involvements for the Partenopei this season.

While speculation has been stirred up about De Bruyne's future, fan favourite Scott McTominay is set to stay put for now, and he has found the net three times in two games against Torino.

McTominay's international teammate Che Adams is Toro's leading Serie A scorer on four; the Scotland striker could partner Giovanni Simeone, who only scored six times in 83 league appearances for Napoli but has previously scored five goals against them.

Typically lining up just behind the front pair, Nikola Vlasic missed Sunday's clash between Croatia and the Czech Republic due to a minor thigh strain, but he is still expected to play this weekend.

However, Abate has fitness doubts regarding wing-backs Rafik Belghali, Ricardo Rodriguez and Niccolo Fortini.

After two defeats and one draw from their last three games, both teams will be desperate for a win.

While Napoli are hampered by injuries and appear disunited, Torino have been leaking too many goals, so more frustration could be on the cards.

#2042. GdS: Maignan’s message, Tomori and Loftus-Cheek – the latest on Milan’s injuries

The AC Milan squad returned to training at Milanello on Monday, at least those who are not with their national team.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) has provided an update on the various injuries that have massively depleted the depth available to head coach Ruben Amorim in the past few weeks.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Starting with Mike Maignan, both he and the French medical staff have reassured Milan regarding the physical issue that forced the goalkeeper to be substituted at half-time during Sunday’s match between Les Bleus and Turkey.

The Rossoneri captain took a knock to the hip area and felt some discomfort in his right adductor. No medical examinations were conducted while he was away, but they have been scheduled for early this afternoon.

Maignan has put the club at ease, stating that he is not in any pain. Yesterday evening, he posted a photo of himself preparing to make a save, perhaps a way of saying he is ready. However, Lorenzo Torriani is on stand-by if needed.

Having left for the international break on a rare low, Como will aim to resume their stellar start to the season when Cagliari visit Stadio Sinigaglia on Saturday.

Not only are the Lariani making a big impact in Europe, they have been breaking new ground in Serie A - but defeat to the champions recently slowed their charge towards the top four.

Como have caught the eye in this season's Champions League - notably following their famous 4-1 defeat of Manchester United with a ruthless 9-1 destruction of Lens - and they also have big ambitions in Serie A.

Remarkably, the European rookies sit above Barcelona and Bayern Munich in UEFA's top competition, and they had posted six straight wins across all competitions before facing Inter Milan last time out.

Overseen by one of football's most-wanted coaches, the Lariani scored 22 goals and conceded just four during that hot streak, but it came to an abrupt end at San Siro.

Como's 12th consecutive league defeat to Inter left Cesc Fabregas and co five points behind the Scudetto holders, while costing them their place in the top four.

As a manager, Fabregas has yet to conquer Inter in either Serie A or the Coppa Italia, but his team tend to take care of business against Italy's lesser lights.

Now heading back to base, Como have kept clean sheets in their last three league matches at the Sinigaglia, where they have never lost a top-flight clash against Cagliari.

Beaten 2-1 when the pair most recently met, Cagliari's last Serie A win over Como dates back to March 1982 - albeit both clubs have spent plenty of time outside the top tier.

This term, the Sardinian side will head to Lombardy full of confidence, as they sit just inside the top half following a largely positive start to the current campaign.

Hurtling out of the blocks, Fabio Pisacane's men claimed four victories from their opening five fixtures - only losing to Inter - before slipping back into the pack with a less successful run.

Yet, when facing down Frosinone after suffering four consecutive defeats, Cagliari came out on top: Michel Adopo's goal gave them a 1-0 win over the newly promoted high-flyers.

All told, a haul of 16 points from their first 11 matches represents the Rossoblu's best top-flight start since 2019, and Pisacane has been handed much of the credit.

Continuing an injury-hit start to his Como career, Moise Kean has suffered a setback in his recovery from a tibia problem and could be sidelined for several more weeks.

Wide men Jayden Addai, Assane Diao and Jesus Rodriguez are also unavailable, but Fabregas hopes to have Trevoh Chalobah back in the squad.

The hosts' star man, Nico Paz helped Argentina beat Costa Rica 7-0 earlier this week, scoring his first international brace.

The 22-year-old has already posted 14 goal involvements for Como this season, attracting interest from Europe's top clubs. Curiously, though, just two of his last 11 Serie A strikes have come on home soil.

While Paz should link up with Greece striker Tasos Douvikas in the final third, Cagliari's front line may be led by Paul Mendy and Daniel Maldini - the latter of whom has found the net five times this term.

Although Pisacane can recall Adam Obert after the left-back served a suspension against Frosinone, several men are still missing through injury.

M'Bala Nzola and Mattia Felici have been ruled out, while Harry Winks (back) and Yerry Mina (thigh) are struggling to return in time.

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:35, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 18:36

Thomas Frank has provided his first injury update as Crystal Palace manager ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash with Coventry City at the CBS Arena.

Nine months after his sacking by Tottenham Hotspur, Frank was appointed the new Eagles boss on Monday, just five days after Pierre Sage was relieved of his duties.

The Dane has taken over a Palace side that sits rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of their opening 10 top-flight fixtures, including a 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool before the international break.

Defender Takehiro Tomiyasu has been sidelined for the last nine matches in all competitions with a calf injury, while last season’s top scorer Ismaila Sarr has been limited to only 15 minutes of Premier League action this term due to an ongoing groin problem.

Speaking at a press conference on Thursday afternoon, Frank confirmed that both players will not be ready to return for the trip to Coventry.

"I can say that Tomiyasu will be back training next week," Frank told reporters. "On Sarr, it'll be touch and go when he can start training. It's a groin injury so you need to be careful.

"You need to be aware with those injuries about how much you push. That could take a little longer time. You need to make sure that you don't take two steps forward, to then take two steps back.

"This could take a little longer. He'll not necessarily be on the pitch next week."

Chadi Riad (knee) remains a long-term injury absentee for Palace, while there was no mention of Jorgen Strand Larsen at Frank’s press conference, but the striker has been spotted in training this week after withdrawing from the Norway squad with an ankle issue.

Meanwhile, striker Jean-Philippe Mateta will serve the second of a three-match suspension this weekend following his red card against Tottenham at the end of last month.

Palace are hoping for an immediate manager bounce under Frank following a disappointing run of four straight defeats in the Premier League.

The Eagles won their first four visits to the CBS Arena between 2005 and 2008, but are winless in their last four across all tournaments between 2009 and their most recent trip in 2012 (D2 L2).

Discussing the challenge of facing Coventry in his first game as Palace boss, Frank said: "I know it'll be difficult.

"But I also trust the boys, I know we'll perform on Saturday. We just need a little margin to go in our favour."

Victory for Palace could see them climb off the foot of the table and out of the relegation zone up to as high as 16th place – above Coventry currently in 17th – if other results go their way this weekend.

#2031. Kasper Hogh and the missed Celtic Christmas advert trick as Martin O’Neill weighs up penalty dilemma

The Celtic Christmas advert was released on Friday containing the usual good cheer and a little festive pop at Rangers. It did, though, miss an obvious storyboard opportunity.

All I want for Christmas is my first Parkhead goal. A sad-looking, shaggy-haired striker is seen traipsing through the snowy streets of the east end of Glasgow before bumping into a dreadlocked king of kings, who gives him the gift of putting the ball in the net.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Although Henrik Larrson is not involved, Kasper Hogh does in fact feature in the latest two-minute festive promo film, which has been released in conjunction with the Celtic FC Foundation’s Christmas appeal.

Callum McGregor calls out “Oi, youse two!” in the direction of Hogh and Benjamin Nygren. Viljami Sinisalo is more direct: “Kasper!” Nygren turns round, and says: “Who?”

It maybe doesn’t work as well when written down. Hogh – pronounced who - is clearly a good sport. However, as Martin O’Neill has said on a number of occasions, and repeated on Friday at Lennoxtown, at some point strikers need to start scoring goals.

Of course, Hogh thought he had finally bagged his first home goal in the hoops two weekends ago. Nygren set him up with a neat pass into the Dane’s path and seconds later the net billowed. Hogh celebrated with understandable gusto before the dismaying news that it was being ruled out for an innocuous foul in the build-up. “For him, that was a killer,” admitted O’Neill on the eve of the latest home game against St Mirren.

All eyes will be on the team sheet. Will Hogh - yet to score after eight Parkhead appearances - play? Having been dropped from the Danish squad for their most recent games against Portugal and Norway, the striker was given some time off in the recent international window.

“He has been here, we have given him some time….he has had no break at all because where he came from (Norway) they were playing matches throughout (the summer),” explained O’Neill.

The manager made an extraordinary – to use one his favourite words - admission following the recent game against Kilmarnock, when Nygren wasted a spot kick. He claimed he would not have let Hogh take the penalty, which visiting keeper Nico Mantl saved, if the Dane had been on the park at the time.

Despite the ever more urgent need for Hogh to break his duck at home, O’Neill clearly felt the potential mental harm from failing to convert from 12 yards would have been too great a risk. The game, with Celtic winning 1-0 at the time, was also on a knife edge. A pressure penalty might not have been what Hogh needed.

It will be interesting to see what happens against St Mirren if Celtic are awarded another penalty and Hogh is available to take it. One might expect the Dane to demand to be given the ball and put this ridiculous issue to bed. Adding to the intrigue is that Nygren, who has an Achilles knock picked up on international duty with Sweden, might not play. Not that O’Neill trusts him from the spot now in any case.

The manager was not a fan of Nygren’s penalty technique against Kilmarnock. “All I will say is that if Nygren plays, which he may or may not, he won’t take it!” he said. “All this (stuttered) walking up….why not just do an Alan Shearer and blast it into the net!? If you hit the goalkeeper, you’ll take his head off!”

Non-scoring strikers is a theme just now given Oli McBurnie’s continued struggles at international level for Scotland. After just being subbed on, one wondered whether Sebastien Pocognoli might have ordered him to take the penalty against North Macedonia at Hampden Park last week. Again, with the manager’s future prospects possibly resting on the kick, maybe not. John McGinn did the necessary and Pocognoli survives, for the time being.

Hogh won’t want any handouts. He’s a centre forward who thrives on goals. He will feel capable of working it out for himself. No charity, please.

As shown against Kilmarnock, he’s not far away. He missed one very good chance shortly after his chalked-off goal when one-on-one with Mantl. “If he had the first goal he would have taken that on another yard,” insisted O’Neill. “But that looked like a man in a real hurry to try and get his first (Celtic Park) goal.”

Easy going and charming, there are still limits to what Hogh can endure. He wouldn’t be human if it wasn’t having an effect.

“He seems philosophical about it at this minute,” O’Neill reported. “He thinks if he is working really hard for the side then he can get in….he should have taken a tip or two from Duran!”

Camilo Duran is the opposite. With 13 goals in 21 appearances, he has made a flying start to his Celtic career.

Or maybe the aforementioned Larsson can make a visit. Like Hogh, the Swede was not an immediate hit at Parkhead.

O’Neill himself suggested Larsson could have some input - “The best thing for me to do is bring Henrik Larsson over and show him how to hit the ball into the net!” - when the discussion turned to players who initially laboured under great expectations.

Perhaps the late Trevor Francis, his old teammate, was one too? O’Neill was at Nottingham Forest when the striker arrived at the City Ground to become Britain’s first £1 million player. Talk about pressure.

“He took a couple of weeks,” remembered O’Neill. “It didn’t help that he had just been signed for a million pounds and Brian Clough told him to make the tea for everyone, which he did!

“First match, he made the tea for us in the dressing room! That wasn’t exactly what Trevor was expecting.” Hogh, who cost eleven times what Clough paid for Francis, has not been made to suffer such indignities - yet.

#2030. Barnsley FC's Arley Kay shows age is just a number, says Cieran Slicker

The Oakwell club's strategy revolves around a young squad of players who can be developed and sold for profit.

At times their inexperience has told, but 18-year-old defender Kay has been one of the success stories this season.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Kay went into Friday's South Yorkshire derby against Sheffield Wednesday a League One ever-present in his debut campaign.

"Massive credit to him," said Slicker, on loan from Ipswich Town.

"He's stepped up from the academy and speaking to him about his story when I first came here, I didn't know who he was. Probably a lot of the other boys didn't.

"He came to train with us in pre-season. I think one thing he did really well – and it's quite tough – is really hold his weight and he's really aggressive in challenges.

"That's something that I've seen and it's helped him a lot. He's been great for us.

"Him being able to play a variety of positions across the backline is really important as well.

"It's probably our responsibility as a team and the club to keep them on the same track because a lot's been made of the young age of the squad."

Slicker is only 24 himself, and thinks too much is made of birth certificates.

"People can speak about age all they want but you look at some of the best players in the world right now," he countered. You don't question Lamine Yamal's age (19).

"You don't question all the other players that are young and playing."
